open_points.subject: bootstrap_first_administrator timestamp source
open_points.text: - bootstrap_first_administrator: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
open_points.question: The behavior requires the value returned by utc_now to be used for every written timestamp, while the existing FIELD_ASSIGNMENT requires an offset-naive UTC timestamp, but utc_now's contract guarantees only datetime and does not guarantee offset-naivety. Must utc_now's contract guarantee an offset-naive UTC datetime, or may bootstrap_first_administrator normalize its result before writing it?
